items.title: 13.8 Reactions of halides with aqueous silver ion followed by aqueous ammonia

blocks.text: Halide ions are identified by two steps: precipitation with aqueous silver nitrate (13.8.1), then testing the solubility of the silver halide in aqueous ammonia (13.8.2). The sequence gives a systematic way to tell the halide ions apart.

blocks.prompt: Describe a simple chemical test to distinguish aqueous potassium bromide from potassium iodide, with reagents and observations (exercise Q.2j).
blocks.explanation: Add aqueous silver nitrate to each: bromide gives a cream precipitate of silver bromide, iodide a pale yellow precipitate of silver iodide. Then add concentrated ammonia: the cream AgBr dissolves to a colourless solution, while the yellow AgI remains undissolved.

items: Silver nitrate test: Ag+ precipitates AgCl (white), AgBr (cream), AgI (yellow); ammonia then distinguishes them by solubility.
